predecessors.name: Kingdom of France
predecessors.text: Tortuga Island and the coast opposite

successors.name: Haiti
successors.text: Cliopatria's Haiti row, 1792-1802, which covers the same western third of Hispaniola (31,347 km2)

ledger.x: 1659: Louis XIV officially establishes the settlement on Tortuga.
1697: Spain recognises French Saint-Domingue at Ryswick.
1777 (3 June): the Treaty of Aranjuez fixes the Hispaniola border and Spain gains the upper Artibonite.
1791 (August): the slave uprising in the North ends the colonial order.

wars.name: Nine Years' War (Treaty of Ryswick)
wars.outcome: Spain recognised French control of Tortuga and the western third of Hispaniola in 1697.

wars.name: Haitian Revolution (opening)
wars.outcome: The August 1791 uprising, abolition in 1793, the British and Spanish invasions, Louverture's takeover of Santo Domingo in January 1801, Leclerc's expedition of 1802 and independence in 1804.

certainty.note: Settlement frontier on Hispaniola, undefined before 1777.
The boundary with Spanish Santo Domingo is fixed by the Treaty of Aranjuez of 3 June 1777, marked by stones.
